title: Fix crash on closed generic structs from referenced assemblies

lines.text: Learn more about using a mix of your own custom formatters and automatically generated ones in [the Analyzer section](#analyzer).

Closed generic types defined in a referenced assembly (for example, `Item<int>` where `Item<T>` is defined in another project or NuGet package) can be used as members of your `[MessagePackObject]` types, including generic value types and record structs.
Diagnostics about the members of such a type are reported by the assembly that defines it rather than by the consuming project, so any problem must be fixed there.

[MagicOnion](https://github.com/Cysharp/MagicOnion) is a code-first gRPC framework based on grpc-dotnet and MessagePack. gRPC usually communicates with Protocol Buffers using IDL. But MagicOnion uses MessagePack for C# and does not need IDL. When communicating C# to C#, schemaless (or rather C# classes as schema) is better than using IDL.
This analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled.
Members of a type defined in a referenced assembly are reported by the project that defines that type, so an unattributed public member of such a type must be fixed in its defining project.

requirement.title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement.intent: A [MessagePackObject] type with a member whose type is a closed generic value type from a referenced assembly must build cleanly and still get a generated resolver.

functional.text: The generator does not throw when a member's type is a closed generic struct or record struct defined in a referenced assembly.
The analyzer does not throw for the same member types.
The compiling assembly gets its generated resolver, as it does when the generic type is declared in the same project.

nonFunctional.text: A failure of the generator or analyzer must not pass silently as a build warning that leaves the assembly without a resolver. (inferred)
Behaviour for generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same project does not change. (inferred)

story.what: The change makes TypeCollector wrap the analyzer's diagnostic callback so that it only reports diagnostics whose location is in a source tree of the compilation being analyzed. It also replaces two places that indexed DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] (one with a hard cast to PropertyDeclarationSyntax) with null-safe lookups, so members that come from metadata no longer throw. Separately, the MsgPack014 check in the analyzer now matches formatter type arguments that are Annotated instead of NotAnnotated. New generator tests compile a defining assembly to a metadata-only image, use closed generic structs and record structs from it as members, and check that there are no diagnostics and that the resolver is generated. README and MsgPack004 docs describe the new reporting behaviour.
story.why: A closed generic struct or record struct from a referenced assembly has members that exist only in metadata and have no syntax. Indexing DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] on those members threw IndexOutOfRangeException in both the generator and the analyzer (MP-2283). The generator failure surfaced only as a warning and left the assembly without a generated resolver.

findings.title: MsgPack014 nullable formatter check reversed, unrelated to the crash
findings.detail: The where clause in SymbolStartAction now collects IMessagePackFormatter<T> interfaces whose reference-type argument is Annotated instead of NotAnnotated. As a result, formatters that already implement IMessagePackFormatter<T?> get the 'Implement IMessagePackFormatter<T?>' warning, and formatters that implement the non-nullable form are no longer warned. This has nothing to do with closed generic structs from referenced assemblies. It breaks N2 (existing analyzer diagnostics must not change), and builds that treat warnings as errors fail for correct code.

findings.title: BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull silently dropped for positional record properties
findings.detail: GetPropertyIdentifierLocation casts the declaring syntax with 'as PropertyDeclarationSyntax'. For a positional record property declared in the user's own project ([property: Key(...)] on a primary-constructor parameter), that syntax is a ParameterSyntax, so the location is null. The new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation filter then drops any diagnostic whose location is not in source. A MsgPack005 error about the user's own code is therefore lost instead of reported. Before this change the hard cast threw, so the problem was at least visible. The MemberNeedsKey path a few lines above already falls back to ParameterSyntax.Identifier; this helper should do the same.

citations.quote: var identifier = (syntax as PropertyDeclarationSyntax)?.Identifier ?? (syntax as ParameterSyntax)?.Identifier;

findings.title: Generator failures can still surface only as a CS8785 warning
findings.detail: N1 asks that a generator or analyzer failure not pass as a build warning that leaves the assembly without a resolver. The fix only removes the specific DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] crash sites. Generator mode (reportDiagnostic is null) has no guard that turns an unexpected exception into an error-level diagnostic, so any other crash on metadata symbols would still produce a CS8785 warning and a missing resolver. Only the new tests assert this; the source has no such guard.

findings.title: No snapshot of generated resolver for cross-assembly generic struct
findings.detail: F3 expects the consuming assembly to get a resolver and formatter, as it does when the generic type is declared in the same project. The new tests use TestBehaviors.SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck and only assert that the resolver hint name exists. They never check that the resolver registers a formatter for MyGenericStruct<int> or Item<int>, or that the generated code is right. A resolver missing that registration would still pass.

findings.title: No round-trip test through the generated resolver
findings.detail: No test serializes and deserializes a [MessagePackObject] that has a closed generic struct member from a referenced assembly through the generated resolver, so F3's runtime behaviour is not verified.

findings.title: Suppression applies to all rules but is documented only for MsgPack004
findings.detail: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops every analyzer diagnostic located outside the compilation, including MsgPack005, 007, 003 and others, not only MsgPack004. Only the MsgPack004 help page describes this. The other affected doc/analyzers pages say nothing about it.
